newsitem.title: UK: Europe physical aluminium demand, premiums pick up.
newsitem.headline: Europe physical aluminium demand, premiums pick up.

text.p: Premiums for physical aluminium edged higher this week, and traders said on Thursday that demand in Europe was brisk.
"We have seen very firm demand in Europe and the States as well," a London-based trader said.
Premiums were firmer against the background of stronger London Metal Exchange (LME) prices, where three months metal spiked up above $1,600 this week amid sizable declines in LME inventories.

"These stock falls are reflected in the rising aluminium premiums - in Rotterdam a month ago ingots were available at $35 (over LME cash) against the current level of $55, if an offer can be found," analyst Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said in a report.
Traders said that most interest centered around Russian A7E, which was quoted at $40/$45 versus $35/42 a week ago, and Western duty-unpaid last at $50/55 compared to $45/$55.
Russian A7E traded at $40 and $41 this week, while Western duty-unpaid traded at $50.
Meanwhile Western duty paid premiums were quoted at $130/$137, some $5 higher than a week ago.
Russian A5, A6 and A0 remained in short supply, trader said.
In the physical copper market, meanwhile, premiums were mostly steady. But traders were expecting them to ease if this week's explosion in nearby backwardation in LME metal persisted.

Demand for standard Russian metal, which traded at $15 below LME, may be escalating as players try to pre-empt tightness forecast for mid-May when the northern Dudinka port traditionally closes due to flooding.
